messages.content: The Phoenix audit is behind me, so I want to start the Puerto Vallarta vacation. We can travel Saturday, November 7 through Friday, November 13, or Saturday, November 28 through Friday, December 4. It will be six nights for two adults from San Francisco. Compare the whole trip, not just room rates.

I’ll compare both 2026 windows using round-trip airfare for two, six hotel nights with taxes and mandatory fees, airport transfers, and meals not included by the resort. Before I price it, should I keep the three properties we discussed conceptually: a beachfront resort with breakfast and transfers bundled, a lower flexible room rate with meals separate, and an adults-only resort with the better pool and spa setup?
Yes. I want to see whether the bundles are actually worth it. Include deposits, cancellation deadlines, beach access, and whether we can realistically get two massages.

For November 7-13, the best practical nonstop flights are currently $1,148 total for two, including standard economy seats and one checked bag each. The adults-only property pairs poorly with that schedule because the available nonstop return leaves early enough to lose most of Friday; the better-timed itinerary connects once and costs $878 total. For November 28-December 4, well-timed nonstops total $936 for two. I’m checking the resort terms against those flight options now.
Use the better-timed flights. An early return that effectively removes the last day is not a fair comparison.

Understood. Here is the first complete pass. For November 7-13: the beachfront breakfast-and-transfer package is $4,740, plus $1,148 flights and about $1,080 for lunches and dinners, totaling $6,968. The flexible resort is $3,312 including taxes and its resort fee, plus $1,148 flights, $80 transfers, and about $1,500 for meals, totaling $6,040. The adults-only resort is $5,760 on an all-inclusive rate, plus the better-timed one-stop flights at $878, $96 transfers, and $440 for two massages, totaling $7,174.
And the later week? Also, are you counting spa treatments at either of the first two?

The later week prices better overall. The beachfront package is $5,010, flights are $936, and unbundled lunches and dinners are estimated at $1,080, for $7,026. The flexible resort is $3,060, plus $936 flights, $80 transfers, and $1,500 for meals, for $5,576. The adults-only all-inclusive rate is $5,340, plus $936 flights, $96 transfers, and $440 for two massages, for $6,812. I included massages only for the adults-only option; adding comparable treatments to either of the first two would add roughly $410-$470.
The beachfront package gets more expensive later even though the flights drop. What exactly is included there?

Its $5,010 later-week package includes an ocean-view king room, taxes, daily breakfast for two, and private round-trip airport transfers. It does not include lunch, dinner, alcohol, spa services, or gratuities. The resort opens directly onto the beach, with loungers and towel service for guests. A $2,505 deposit is due when booked. The balance is charged 30 days before arrival, and cancellation is refundable through October 29; after that, the deposit becomes nonrefundable.
That is a significant deposit for a breakfast-only package. Give me the same level of detail on the flexible resort.

The flexible option is $3,060 for the later week, including a king room, tax, and mandatory resort fee. Breakfast is about $32 per person, lunch about $25, and dinner about $58 before drinks and gratuity; the $1,500 meal allowance assumes a mix of resort meals and several meals in town. A private transfer is $80 round trip, while taxis should be slightly less. The booking takes a one-night deposit of $510, refundable if canceled by November 21. The remaining balance is paid at checkout.
How is its beach? I do not want a listing that says beachfront when the usable swimming area is somewhere else.

It is genuinely beachfront: the pool terrace leads directly to a sandy hotel beach without crossing a road or taking a shuttle. The swimming area is usually usable, but conditions can vary and the sand is narrower than at the bundled resort. The bundled property has the better beach setup and a broader maintained section. Both provide loungers; neither guarantees calm water every day.
Now the adults-only property. The total is better than the beachfront package later, but I remember it may not really be on the beach.

Correct. The adults-only property sits uphill, so it does not offer walk-out beach access. Guests use a dedicated beach club reached by a frequent shuttle in about 8-10 minutes, and returning involves the shuttle or a steep uphill walk. Its strengths are two quieter pools, an adults-only rooftop pool, and the most extensive spa of the three. The $5,340 rate includes meals and standard beverages but not airport transfers, spa treatments, premium wine, or gratuities.
Can the spa actually take both of us during the later week, preferably at the same time? I do not want to choose it based on a theoretical amenity.

The spa currently shows two 80-minute massage appointments available together at 10:30 a.m. on Monday, November 30, and again at 2:00 p.m. on Wednesday, December 2. The quoted combined price is $440 including the service charge. Appointment holds expire after 24 hours and require a card guarantee; cancellation inside 24 hours is charged in full.
What are the room deposit and cancellation terms there?

The adults-only rate requires a $2,670 deposit at booking, with the balance due 21 days before arrival. It is refundable through October 30. From October 31 through November 6, the penalty is the deposit; after November 6, the full stay is nonrefundable. The spa guarantee is separate and would not be charged now unless the appointments are missed or canceled late.

The later week seems right. It has the best nonstop fare and avoids the compromised flight schedule. Between the flexible resort and adults-only resort, show me what the extra $1,236 buys. Do not keep the breakfast bundle in the final pair.

For the additional $1,236, the adults-only option replaces the flexible resort’s estimated meal budget with an all-inclusive plan, adds a quieter adults-only atmosphere, offers substantially stronger pools and spa facilities, and includes the two massages in the comparison total. The tradeoffs are the $2,670 deposit, an earlier cancellation deadline, and shuttle access to the beach. The flexible resort keeps $2,160 more of the trip cost outside the initial deposit and gives you direct beach access, more freedom to eat in town, and cancellation through November 21, but its pools and spa are more conventional.
Keep November 28 through December 4 and those two resorts. I am not ready to book, but give me the exact comparison I can discuss with my spouse, including what would be due now.

Shortlist for November 28-December 4, 2026, for two adults from SFO:

Flexible beachfront resort: $936 nonstop flights, $3,060 room with taxes and resort fee, $80 private transfers, and a $1,500 meal allowance. Estimated trip total: $5,576 before alcohol, gratuities, and spa services. Due to reserve the room now: $510. The room remains refundable through November 21. It has direct access to a usable sandy beach and standard resort pools; meals can be taken at the resort or in town.

Adults-only spa resort: $936 nonstop flights, $5,340 all-inclusive room, $96 transfers, and $440 for two simultaneous 80-minute massages. Estimated trip total: $6,812 before gratuities, premium beverages, and off-property meals. Due to reserve the room now: $2,670; the massage appointments require a card guarantee but no advance charge. The room is refundable through October 30. It has the strongest pool and spa offering, with simultaneous massage openings on November 30 and December 2, but its beach club requires an 8-10 minute shuttle.

The later week is selected, the breakfast-and-transfer property is removed from consideration, and nothing has been booked.
